author_reading.workflow_class: Gray pointer FIFO and cross-clock memory
author_reading.rationale: Both clocks access the same fixed memory location continuously; the independent clocks can collide on a write and read, and the RTL has no collision policy.

rationale: mem[0] is written every clk_a edge and sampled every asynchronous clk_b edge. No ownership, stable-data interval or collision exclusion exists. A memory declaration alone supplies no safe concurrent same-address contract; the destination can capture incoherent or metastable data.

labels.workflow_class: Gray pointer FIFO and cross-clock memory
labels.rationale: The same mem[0] is written on every clk_a edge and read on every asynchronous clk_b edge, without ownership, stable-data qualification, or a collision policy. This RTL describes continuously changing cross-domain storage, not an established safe dual-clock memory contract. Coincident or nearby writes can corrupt the captured word. The memory implementation is also unresolved; that does not make the unconditional unsafe transfer safe.

labels.workflow_class: Gray pointer FIFO and cross-clock memory
labels.rationale: Both domains continuously access the same constant memory address. There is no ownership, valid qualification, stability interval or collision exclusion. Concurrent write/read can capture incoherent or metastable data; declaring a memory does not make this direct bus crossing safe.
